sentences.cn_text: 纽约爱乐乐团决定聘任艾伦·吉尔伯特担任下一任音乐总监，自2009年突然宣布这一任命以来，一直是古典音乐界热议的话题。
sentences.en_text: The decision of the New York Philharmonic to hire Alan Gilbert as its next music director has been the talk of the classical-music world ever since the sudden announcement of his appointment in 2009.

sentences.cn_text: 总体而言，反响至少可以说是相当积极的。「太好了！」
sentences.en_text: For the most part, the response has been favorable, to say the least. “Hooray!

sentences.cn_text: 「终于等到了！」一位严肃的古典音乐评论家安东尼·托马西尼写道。
sentences.en_text: At last!” wrote Anthony Tommasini, a sober-sided classical-music critic.

sentences.cn_text: 然而，这一任命之所以如此出人意料，原因之一在于吉尔伯特相对而言并不太知名。
sentences.en_text: One of the reasons why the appointment came as such a surprise, however, is that Gilbert is comparatively little known.

sentences.cn_text: 即便是曾在《纽约时报》上支持任命吉尔伯特的托马西尼，也称他为「一位朴实无华的音乐家,身上没有那种令人望而生畏的指挥家气势」。
sentences.en_text: Even Tommasini, who had advocated Gilbert’s appointment in the Times, calls him “an unpretentious musician with no air of the formidable conductor about him.”

sentences.cn_text: 作为对一个迄今为止一直由古斯塔夫·马勒和皮埃尔·布列兹这样的音乐家执掌的乐团的下一任音乐总监的描述，这似乎很可能让至少部分《纽约时报》读者觉得是意味寡淡的褒扬。
sentences.en_text: As a description of the next music director of an orchestra that has hitherto been led by musicians like Gustav Mahler and Pierre Boulez, that seems likely to have struck at least some Times readers as faint praise.

sentences.cn_text: 就我而言，我无从判断吉尔伯特是否是一位伟大的指挥家，抑或哪怕是一位优秀的指挥家。
sentences.en_text: For my part, I have no idea whether Gilbert is a great conductor or even a good one.

sentences.cn_text: 诚然，他演绎了种类丰富且颇具趣味的作品，但我并不需要前往艾弗里·费舍尔音乐厅或任何其他地方去聆听有趣的管弦乐。
sentences.en_text: To be sure, he performs an impressive variety of interesting compositions, but it is not necessary for me to visit Avery Fisher Hall, or anywhere else, to hear interesting orchestral music.

sentences.cn_text: 我只需走到CD架前，或者打开电脑从iTunes下载更多录制音乐即可。
sentences.en_text: All I have to do is to go to my CD shelf, or boot up my computer and download still more recorded music from iTunes.

sentences.cn_text: 那些回应称录音无法替代现场演出的忠实音乐会听众并未领会要点。
sentences.en_text: Devoted concertgoers who reply that recordings are no substitute for live performance are missing the point.

sentences.cn_text: 为了争夺热爱艺术的公众的时间、注意力和金钱,古典器乐演奏家不仅要与歌剧院、舞蹈团、剧院团体和博物馆竞争,还要与20世纪伟大古典音乐家的录音演出竞争。
sentences.en_text: For the time, attention, and money of the art-loving public, classical instrumentalists must compete not only with opera houses, dance troupes, theater companies, and museums, but also with the recorded performances of the great classical musicians of the 20th century.

sentences.cn_text: 这些录音价格低廉、随处可得,而且艺术质量往往远高于当今的现场演出;此外,听众还可以在自己选择的时间和地点「消费」它们。
sentences.en_text: These recordings are cheap, available everywhere, and very often much higher in artistic quality than today’s live performances; moreover, they can be “consumed” at a time and place of the listener’s choosing.

sentences.cn_text: 此类录音的广泛可得性因而给传统古典音乐会这一体制带来了危机。
sentences.en_text: The widespread availability of such recordings has thus brought about a crisis in the institution of the traditional classical concert.

sentences.cn_text: 一种可能的应对之策是让古典音乐演奏者编排尚未录制成唱片的、具有吸引力的新曲目。
sentences.en_text: One possible response is for classical performers to program attractive new music that is not yet available on record.

sentences.cn_text: 吉尔伯特本人对新音乐的兴趣已被广泛关注:古典音乐评论家亚历克斯·罗斯形容他是一个能够将爱乐乐团变成「一个明显不同、更具活力的组织」的人。
sentences.en_text: Gilbert’s own interest in new music has been widely noted: Alex Ross, a classical-music critic, has described him as a man who is capable of turning the Philharmonic into “a markedly different, more vibrant organization.”

sentences.cn_text: 但这种不同的本质将会是什么呢？
sentences.en_text: But what will be the nature of that difference?

sentences.cn_text: 仅仅拓展乐团的曲目库是不够的。
sentences.en_text: Merely expanding the orchestra’s repertoire will not be enough.

sentences.cn_text: 如果吉尔伯特和爱乐乐团想要取得成功,他们必须首先改变美国这一历史最悠久的乐团与其希望吸引的新受众之间的关系。
sentences.en_text: If Gilbert and the Philharmonic are to succeed, they must first change the relationship between America’s oldest orchestra and the new audience it hopes to attract.
